resolutions.what_changed: The ceiling moved out of the case and into the runner. evals/run.py now holds WALL_BUDGET_S = {"fast": 60} and a pure over_budget(suite, wall_seconds), applies it to totals["wall_seconds"] of the run it has just finished, prints a named line and returns 1 — the same shape as the invariant-100% rule beside it. No report file is involved, so a fresh CI clone and a --no-report pre-commit run are both covered. fast-wall-clock-budget no longer reads evals/report/ at all; it grades the ruling: the 60.00/60.01 boundary, that `fast` is the only suite carrying a ceiling, and that the constant still equals the ADR's number.
resolutions.watched_red: Case rewritten and run before over_budget existed: `[FAIL] fast-wall-clock-budget`, 88/89 = 0.989 against baseline 1.000, `ImportError: cannot import name 'WALL_BUDGET_S' from 'evals.run'`.
resolutions.repro_after_fix: The reviewer's own repro, replayed against the repaired tree (0.25s added per case inside the runner's timed region, no repo file edited, --no-report): `[eval] OVER BUDGET: suite 'fast' wall clock 78.42s > 60s (ADR-002 Decision 4)` and exit 1. Before the repair the same slowdown gave 89/89 = 1.000 and exit 0.
resolutions.note_for_reviewer: One detail found while reproducing: totals["wall_seconds"] is the SUM of per-case `seconds`, not true elapsed, so a slowdown injected outside run_case is invisible to it (measured: sum 55.49s for a run whose real elapsed was ~78s). The two agree to ~0.1% on a normal run because the runner does almost nothing between cases. Not changed here — it would move every historical number in the reports — and stated rather than papered over.
